summary: The article reports on a September 5, 2023 symposium on "Educational Outreach and Engagement for Sustainable Living" and related events, arguing that education is the foundation of environmental conservation. It covers school curricula, educational public spaces, hands-on learning, community workshops, business involvement and digital campaigns. It closes by stressing the need for sustained funding and community-wide engagement.
one_line: A local symposium and related events promote environmental education through schools, public spaces, workshops, businesses and digital campaigns, while calling for sustained funding.
key_facts: The symposium on "Educational Outreach and Engagement for Sustainable Living" took place on September 5, 2023, at the Maplewood Community Hall.
Ecologist Dr. Susan Chang spearheaded the symposium, declaring "We feed the mind to nurture the earth."
The approach aims to integrate sustainable living concepts into curricula from kindergarten to college.

Urban planner Emily Rivera presented educational public spaces on September 20, 2023, at the Green Spaces Forum, including parks with plaques on native plants and community gardens with QR codes linking to composting videos.
High school biology teacher Mark Johnson has led the Practical Science Initiative since October 3, 2023, pushing for more field trips and hands-on experiments such as water quality tests.
Margaret Lee, founder of the NGO Green Neighbors, called community workshops "a bridge" connecting the theoretical to the practical.
Example workshops include seminars on energy-efficient appliances and classes on bike repair.
EcoTech Innovations has organized eco-fairs and sustainability seminars for the community.
EcoTech CEO David Hilbert spoke at an October 15, 2023 green business conference, saying education is as crucial for employees as for school children.
Social media strategist Diane Brooks said "Digital is the lever we need to amplify our message."
Brooks' team has worked since late September on interactive, gamified campaigns that reward users for adopting sustainable practices.
A recurring theme at the symposium was the need for sustained funding through grants, donations and government backing.
Local policymakers were urged to consider the long-term benefits of investing in environmental education when planning budgets.
